partition_note_on_ruling_17.issue: Six rows in this partition are partial-refresh residue in living documents, and I have split them 2 ways. The split is deliberate and is the main judgement call in this pass.
partition_note_on_ruling_17.rule_applied: Ruling 17 books as SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE 'a clause faithful when written whose artefact later moved'. I read that as requiring the clause's truth-conditions to have been falsified by the ARTEFACT moving. Where a later edit to the DOCUMENT imported the moved values and left the label describing them, the clause was falsified by the document's own act, and ruling 14's 'wrong at its own era' applies with the document's era = its last revision.
partition_note_on_ruling_17.consequence: 083#8[0] (4,744 GT features) books as SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE — the clause annotates an external input file whose drift the 2026-05-03 edit did not cause. 083#5[0]/#11[0]/#56[0]/#63[0] (bootstrap 1,000) book as DOC-DEFECT-AT-ERA — those clauses label the CIs printed in §2, and fc536a19c replaced those CIs with 10,000-iteration BCa values in the same commit that left the labels alone.
partition_note_on_ruling_17.if_the_PI_reads_ruling_17_more_broadly: All four bootstrap rows in 083 flip to SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE and the counts become SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE 21 / DOC-DEFECT-AT-ERA 3 (the survivors being 086#22[0], 086#37[0] and 083#46[4], none of which involve drift of any kind). The repair is identical either way (living-doc fix to 10,000 / BCa). What changes is whether the record states that a paper-citation document misdescribed its own Methods for fifteen months. I recommend it should.
partition_note_on_ruling_17.not_affected: The four 087 rows in ci-metadata-registry.md are unambiguous under either reading — those lines were never re-edited after the migration.

named_residuals_and_escalations.title: CI metadata sidecars were never migrated and now contradict their own targets
named_residuals_and_escalations.detail: The N=10K commits (fe21fe6c2, 6b611174c) and the BCa commits (bae12aa96, 85f115015) touched only evaluation.{json,csv,md} — verified by git show --stat. The co-located evaluation.metadata.json sidecars were not touched. Today results/gold-standard-extended-buffer-sweep/evaluation.json records _metadata.bootstrap = {n_iterations: 10000, method: BCa} while its sibling evaluation.metadata.json records {n_iterations: 1000, methodology: 'percentile bootstrap'}. Same for all three archived cleaned-GT sidecars. results/ci-metadata-registry.md designates these sidecars as the AUTHORITY for its YES_SIDECAR rows — so the registry's stated authority is itself corrupt for every cell touched by the migration.
named_residuals_and_escalations.scope_estimate: ad023fc3b wrote 48 sidecars; the migration touched an unknown subset. Needs a mechanical sweep comparing each *.metadata.json bootstrap block against its sibling evaluation.json _metadata.bootstrap block. This is cheap and fully deterministic.
named_residuals_and_escalations.why_it_matters: This is not a documentation problem — it is a provenance artefact asserting a false parameter about the file next to it, in the exact layer the charter §4 hierarchy treats as more authoritative than prose.

named_residuals_and_escalations.title: Instrument: era_check is still gated on ruling 12's superseded dated-filename rule
named_residuals_and_escalations.detail: scripts/recompute_c4_claims.py defines SNAPSHOT_STEM_RE = /\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}|session-\d+/ over the filename stem and attaches era_check only when it matches. Across the whole 16,083-row recompute report, era_check fired on 308 rows in 11 documents, all with dated stems. It fired on ZERO of my 24 rows. Yet 22 of my 24 verdicts turned entirely on per-claim era-faithfulness, which I had to establish by hand with git log -L and git show on every anchor. Ruling 14 demoted the presentation class to ADVISORY ONLY and made per-claim era-faithfulness THE deciding axis; the harness still implements the provisional rule ruling 14 superseded.
named_residuals_and_escalations.recommendation: Attach era_check to every MISMATCH row on a read/arithmetic method, gated on nothing. Resolve the anchor at the source LINE's last-touch commit (git log -L <line>,<line>:<file>) as well as the document's last commit — the two differ for exactly the partial-refresh-residue class, and the difference is what distinguishes ruling 17 divergence from a ruling 14 defect. This is the highest-leverage instrument change available for the remaining waves; it would have mechanically produced 20 of my 24 verdicts.

rows_not_fitting_any_account.note: All 24 rows fit one of the four causal accounts A–D. The partition does NOT share a single cause: A (recovery/GT drift, 13 rows) and B (bootstrap migration, 8 rows) are independent upstream events three days apart; C (registry row conflation, 2 rows) involves no drift whatsoever and predates both; D (double rounding, 1 row) is an authoring slip in a single table cell. Two of the four accounts produce DOC-DEFECT-AT-ERA verdicts and two produce SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE — except account B, which produces BOTH depending on whether the host document was re-edited after the migration. That split is the finding I would most want a second reader to check.

research_conclusion_moves.statement: No row in this partition requires a research conclusion to move. The MCC report's rank orderings, its F1/MCC divergence finding (Obs 280 confirmation), text-MIN's bottom placement at every buffer, the corrected-F1 >= 0.830 claim, and the 55-map-vs-4-map generalisation gap all survive every correction. What does move is Methods text: the paper must state 10,000 bootstrap iterations with BCa intervals (not 1,000 percentile) for the 55-map MCC family and for the cleaned-GT and gold-standard extended-buffer evaluations; the pairwise effect-size family is 54 comparisons, not 52; and the Era-1 tiered leaderboard covers 36 conditions of 72 input, not 19.
